findings.title: Owner verdicts do not require verified owned-process cleanup and stopped Playwright
findings.observed: The analyzer requires browserClosed but ignores ownedCleanup.verified, ownedCleanup.remaining and playwrightStopped. The driver labels a 16-slot result RAW_BATCH_RETURNED and may exit zero even when owned cleanup failed and the lock remains held.
findings.control: Starting from the supplied valid synthetic batch, set playwrightStopped=false and ownedCleanup={verified:false,remaining:[one identity]}. The callback owner still returns PASS with no global reason.
findings.consequence: An acquisition lacking the promised cleanup proof can still issue a numeric owner PASS or FAIL. This is a lifecycle/qualification defect, not an observed real orphan or native cost regression.
findings.minimalRepair: Require explicit stopped Playwright, verified owned cleanup and empty remaining identities before numeric owner verdicts. Missing, false or contradictory cleanup fields must yield INCOMPLETE. Make batch/exit disposition agree with cleanup failure while retaining the resource lock.
findings.targetedControl: Exercise each missing/false cleanup field and a contradictory verified=true/nonempty-remaining record. Retain one valid-cleanup positive control.

findings.title: Later process snapshots erase previously observed owned identities
findings.observed: owned is assigned from the current descendant snapshot at launch and each slot; the final union includes only the latest assignment and the final snapshot. It is not a cumulative history.
findings.control: A deterministic data-flow control gives the first snapshot one PID/create-time/executable identity and a later snapshot none. The current assignment retains zero identities.
findings.consequence: If a previously observed child outlives its driver and disappears from the current descendant tree, that identity may never reach the final exact-identity reaper. An empty reaper input can then appear verified. This is a reachable source path, not evidence that an orphan actually occurred.
findings.minimalRepair: Maintain a cumulative map of PID and create-time with executable identity at every observation. Absence from a later descendant snapshot must not erase the earlier identity. Resolve its current identity/liveness during bounded cleanup; never terminate a reused or unrelated PID.
findings.targetedControl: Use mocked process observations to retain an orphaned earlier identity, reject PID reuse/executable mismatch and verify already-dead identities without real process enumeration or termination.

findings.title: Fully contained sampling censors slow callbacks crossing the window end
findings.observed: Steady samples require both start within the window and completion by start+5000 ms. Boundary straddlers are counted but do not prevent a numeric PASS.
findings.control: For every slot with window 5010..10010 ms, place five calls at 5110, 6110, 7110, 8110 and 10009.8. A calls all last 0.1 ms; B last call lasts 1.0 ms and the end mark is 10011 ms. The analyzer keeps A=40 and B=32 calls, reports paired p95 PASS in all rounds and owner PASS. Including all calls starting inside the window gives A p95=0.1, B p95=1.0, delta=0.9 ms versus 0.25 ms allowance.
findings.consequence: The outcome-dependent filter can remove the very slow calls the p95 is supposed to detect. The existing rate diagnostic does not catch this control: 1.0 versus 0.8 Hz is at its 0.2 Hz floor.
findings.minimalRepair: Select every actual synchronous call with start >= windowStart and start < windowStart+5000, retaining its full inclusive and exclusive duration even if completion crosses the end. Admit no new starts after that boundary. Keep the existing <=250 ms end-readback lateness bound and retain crossing/late-completion diagnostics.
findings.targetedControl: Retain the slow final-call control; add start-exactly-at-end exclusion and start-before-window exclusion. Do not shorten durations or invoke extra callbacks.

findings.title: Unexplained same-side noise is overridden by a definitive FAIL
findings.observed: The verdict chooses FAIL before checking whether same-side block spread exceeds the adopted allowance.
findings.control: With A=0.1 ms throughout, B=0.1 ms in rounds 0..2 and B=1.0 ms in round 3, the unexplained B spread is 0.9 ms versus 0.25 ms allowance. The current result is FAIL, although the adopted protocol requires an unexplained-noise disposition.
findings.consequence: This is a false definitive classification, not a false PASS. It conflicts with the pre-measurement rule that unresolved noise remains INCOMPLETE and a valid repeatable breach earns FAIL.
findings.minimalRepair: Apply integrity/state/noise validity before a definitive owner status. Preserve raw pooled and paired descriptive breaches, but mark an owner with unresolved above-budget spread INCOMPLETE. Retain the original one explained-repeat ceiling and no automatic search for a pass.
findings.targetedControl: The one-noisy-round fixture must be INCOMPLETE with its descriptive breach retained; a stable repeated breach must remain FAIL and a stable within-budget control PASS.
